# Story 13 — Ticket Core: creation, classification, custom fields, tags, search and history (Story: 460)

Tickets reference `customers.id`, so the customers migrations must be applied before this story's migrations run.

- The shared API layer is in place: `app/Support/Http/ApiResponse.php`, `app/Support/Http/CollectionQuery.php`, `app/Support/Http/CollectionQuerySpec.php`, `app/Support/Http/Errors/ErrorCode.php`, `app/Support/Http/Errors/ApiExceptionRenderer.php`, `app/Http/Middleware/EnforceIdempotency.php`.
- The bilingual layer is in place: `app/Support/I18n/BilingualString.php` and `app/Support/I18n/Casts/BilingualStringCast.php` (used for category names).
- The `app/Domains/Ticketing/` package already exists as **empty scaffolding** (`Actions/`, `Data/`, `Events/`, `Http/`, `Jobs/`, `Listeners/`, `Models/`, `Policies/`, `Services/` are all empty directories). This story fills `Models/`, `Actions/`, `Http/`, `Policies/`, `Services/`.
- Coordinate with the owner of `database/seeders/TicketCatalogueSeeder.php` and `database/seeders/SlaPolicySeeder.php` — both already exist and will need the tables introduced here. This story **must not** break `database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.php` idempotency (see `tests/Feature/Seeders/DatabaseSeederIdempotencyTest.php`).

## Story Goal

Make a support ticket a first-class, tracked domain object.

1. An agent can create a ticket for a customer with a **department** and a **priority**; assignment to a user is optional (a ticket may be unassigned).
2. Every ticket gets a **unique, never-reused reference** in a defined, human-quotable format.
3. Tickets are classified against a **bilingual category tree of at most three levels**; a category may declare **custom fields** that are captured at creation time and validated against the category definition.
4. Free-form **tags** can be attached to a ticket and used as a list filter.
5. `GET /api/v1/tickets` follows the existing collection contract (`CollectionQuery` / `CollectionQuerySpec`), supports **saved views**, and returns status/priority **counts in `meta`**.
6. Ticket **search** matches subject, body and reference and reuses the same Arabic normalisation used by customer search (`app/Domains/Customers/Services/ArabicTextNormaliser.php`).
7. Every meaningful mutation writes a row to a **first-class `ticket_events` history table** (actor, event type, changed fields, timestamp). History is never derived from `updated_at`.

**Not in scope:** SLA timers and breach calculation, ticket comments/conversation threads, channel ingestion (email/portal), assignment routing rules, notifications, escalations, reporting aggregates. Those live in `app/Domains/Sla/`, `app/Domains/Channels/`, `app/Domains/Automation/`, `app/Domains/Reporting/` and are separate stories. Only leave `// TODO(BE-xx)` comments where a hook is obviously needed.

## Product rules (from story)

| Rule | Current behaviour | New behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Ticket existence | No ticket table or model; `app/Domains/Ticketing/` is empty scaffolding | `tickets` table + `Ticket` model with customer, department, priority mandatory; `assigned_user_id` **nullable** |
| Reference | None | Unique, never-reused reference string in a defined format, allocated by a dedicated service backed by a counter table |
| Classification | None | `ticket_categories` bilingual tree, **max depth 3**, `is_active` flag; depth enforced on write |
| Custom fields | None | `ticket_category_fields` definitions + per-ticket `custom_fields` JSON validated against the category chain at creation |
| Tags | None | `ticket_tags` + `ticket_tag_ticket` pivot; free-form, normalised, filterable |
| List | None | Standard collection contract + saved views + status/priority counts in `meta` |
| Search | Customer search only | `q` matches subject, body and reference using the same Arabic normalisation as customer search |
| History | N/A | First-class `ticket_events` table written on every meaningful change; **never** derived from `updated_at` |

#### Create file: `database/migrations/2026_08_26_100100_create_ticket_categories_table.php`

```php
Schema::create('ticket_categories', function (Blueprint $table) {
    $table->id();
    $table->uuid('uuid')->unique();
    $table->foreignId('parent_id')->nullable()->constrained('ticket_categories')->cascadeOnDelete();
    $table->string('code', 64)->unique();
    $table->string('name_en', 255);
    $table->string('name_ar', 255);

    $table->unsignedInteger('position')->default(0);
    $table->boolean('is_active')->default(true)->index();
    $table->timestampsTz();

    $table->index(['parent_id', 'position']);
});
```

`name_en` / `name_ar` are the storage columns behind the `BilingualStringCast` — mirror how the existing bilingual catalogues store their columns (grep for `BilingualStringCast` before choosing the column names; if the codebase already uses a single JSON column, follow that instead and note the choice in the migration docblock).

### 3 — Reference allocation

**Create file: `app/Domains/Ticketing/Services/TicketReferenceGenerator.php`**

Defined format: **`TKT-YYYYMM-NNNNNN`** — literal prefix, year-month period, zero-padded 6-digit sequence (e.g. `TKT-202608-000042`). Document the format in a class docblock.

```php
public function next(?CarbonInterface $at = null): string;
```

Implementation contract:

- Wrap in `DB::transaction`.
- `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` the `ticket_references` row for the period via `lockForUpdate()`; insert it with `last_sequence = 0` when absent.
- Increment `last_sequence`, persist, format and return.
- **Never** derive the sequence from `count(tickets)` or `max(id)` — deleted tickets must not free a reference. The `tickets.reference` unique index is the last line of defence.
- SQLite (used by `database/database.sqlite` and the test suite) ignores `lockForUpdate`; the surrounding transaction plus the unique index still guarantee correctness. Note this in a comment.

Bind nothing in the container — the class is concrete and resolved by autowiring.

### 4 — Category tree and custom-field validation

**Create file: `app/Domains/Ticketing/Services/TicketCategoryTree.php`**

- `maxDepth(): int` returning `3`.
- `assertCanNest(?TicketCategory $parent): void` — throws `TicketCategoryDepthExceededException` when `$parent?->depth >= 3`.
- `resolveFieldDefinitions(TicketCategory $category): Collection` — returns the category's own fields **plus** the fields declared by its ancestors, keyed by `key`, child definitions overriding ancestors.

**Create file: `app/Domains/Ticketing/Services/TicketCustomFieldValidator.php`**

- `validate(TicketCategory $category, array $values): array` — returns the sanitised map to store in `tickets.custom_fields`.
- Rejects unknown keys, missing required keys, values whose type does not match the declared `type`, and `select` values not present in `options`.
- Throws `InvalidTicketCustomFieldException` (implements `HasApiErrorCode`) with `errorMeta()` carrying the offending `field` key so the API envelope stays machine-readable — mirror `app/Support/Http/Exceptions/BotProtectionFailedException.php` lines 16–28.
- When the ticket has **no** category, the only valid `custom_fields` payload is empty.

### 6 — Actions

All under `app/Domains/Ticketing/Actions/`, single-purpose invokable/`handle()` classes matching `app/Domains/Customers/Actions/CreateCustomer.php` and `UpdateCustomer.php`.

- **`CreateTicket.php`** — required: `customer`, `department`, `priority`, `subject`, `body`. Optional: `category`, `assignee`, `tags`, `custom_fields`. Steps, all inside one `DB::transaction`:
  1. Reject a **blocked** customer by reusing `App\Domains\Customers\Exceptions\CustomerBlockedException` (the intake guard precedent is `app/Domains/Customers/Services/CustomerIntakeGuard.php` — read it, 959 B, and call it rather than re-implementing the check).
  2. Allocate the reference via `TicketReferenceGenerator::next()`.
  3. Validate `custom_fields` via `TicketCustomFieldValidator`.
  4. Persist with `status = TicketStatus::New`, normalised subject/body, `created_by_user_id = $actor->id`.
  5. Sync tags via `SyncTicketTags`.
  6. Record `TicketEventType::Created` via `RecordTicketEvent`.
- **`UpdateTicket.php`** — computes a **field-level diff** before saving and writes one `Updated` event whose `payload` is `{"changes": {"field": {"from": …, "to": …}}}`. Only changed fields appear. When nothing changed, **no event is written**.
- **`ReclassifyTicket.php`** — changes category, re-validates custom fields against the new category, drops values whose keys no longer exist, writes `Reclassified` with old/new category uuid in the payload.
- **`AssignTicket.php`** / **`UnassignTicket.php`** — write `Assigned` / `Unassigned` with the target user uuid.
- **`ChangeTicketPriority.php`**, **`ChangeTicketStatus.php`** — write `PriorityChanged` / `StatusChanged` with `from`/`to`.
- **`AddTicketTag.php`**, **`RemoveTicketTag.php`**, **`SyncTicketTags.php`** — tags are free-form: `firstOrCreate` on `name_normalised` (normalised with the same `TextNormaliser`), so "الدعم" and "الدعم " collapse to one tag. Write `TagAdded` / `TagRemoved` per tag.
- **`CreateTicketCategory.php`**, **`UpdateTicketCategory.php`** — call `TicketCategoryTree::assertCanNest()` before saving; recompute `depth` from the parent.
- **`SaveTicketView.php`**, **`DeleteTicketView.php`** — persist the whitelisted query payload (see §8).

**Create file: `app/Domains/Ticketing/Services/RecordTicketEvent.php`**

```php
public function handle(Ticket $ticket, TicketEventType $type, ?User $actor, array $payload = []): TicketEvent;
```

Sets `uuid`, `occurred_at = now()`, `actor_user_id = $actor?->id`. **Every** action above routes through this one method — that is what keeps history first-class rather than derived. `actor_user_id` is nullable so system-originated changes are representable.

### 8 — HTTP layer

Controllers under `app/Domains/Ticketing/Http/Controllers/`, requests under `Http/Requests/`, resources under `Http/Resources/` — the exact layout used by `app/Domains/Customers/Http/`.

**Create file: `app/Domains/Ticketing/Http/Controllers/TicketController.php`**

`index`, `show`, `store`, `update`. Mirror `CustomerController.php` lines 35–75: `ApiResponse::collection(...)` for the list (line 42 precedent), `ApiResponse::item(new TicketResource($ticket->load('customer', 'department', 'category', 'assignee', 'tags')))` for show (line 54 precedent), and `ApiResponse::item(new TicketResource($ticket), 201)` for store (line 63 precedent).

The list spec:

```php
$spec = (new CollectionQuerySpec())
    ->withSorts(['created_at', 'updated_at', 'priority', 'status', 'reference'])
    ->withFilters(['status', 'priority', 'department', 'assignee', 'customer', 'category', 'tag'])
    ->withIncludes(['customer', 'department', 'category', 'assignee', 'tags'])
    ->withSearchableColumns(['subject_normalised', 'body_normalised', 'reference']);
```

Then `CollectionQuery::applyTo()` (line 101) and `paginate()` (line 138). Free-text `q` is routed through `TicketSearch::apply()` **before** `applyTo()` so the term is normalised; if `CollectionQuery` already handles `q` against `withSearchableColumns`, normalise the incoming term and let `CollectionQuery` do the matching — read lines 60–140 of `CollectionQuery.php` and pick whichever path exists, do not add a second search mechanism.

**Counts in meta:** run a single grouped aggregate over the *filtered, unpaginated* query:

```php
$counts = (clone $filtered)->reorder()
    ->selectRaw('status, count(*) as total')->groupBy('status')
    ->pluck('total', 'status');
```

Merge `['counts' => ['status' => …, 'priority' => …]]` into the meta passed to `ApiResponse::collection()`. `CollectionQuery::meta()` (line 150) stays untouched.

**Saved views:** `GET /tickets?view={uuid}` loads a `TicketSavedView` owned by the caller (or `is_shared = true`), decodes its `query` JSON and merges it **under** the request's own query parameters (explicit request params win). The stored payload is whitelisted to the same filter/sort/include keys as the spec — **never** interpolate stored values into raw SQL.

**Create files:**

- `TicketCategoryController.php` — `index` (full tree, `children` nested), `store`, `update`, `destroy` (refuse when tickets reference the category; return the conflict error code).
- `TicketTagController.php` — `index` (searchable), `store`/`destroy` on a ticket's tag set.
- `TicketHistoryController.php` — `GET /tickets/{ticket}/history`, paginated, newest first, mirroring `app/Domains/Customers/Http/Controllers/CustomerTimelineController.php`.
- `TicketSavedViewController.php` — `index`, `store`, `destroy` scoped to the authenticated user.

**Requests:** `StoreTicketRequest`, `UpdateTicketRequest`, `AssignTicketRequest`, `StoreTicketCategoryRequest`, `UpdateTicketCategoryRequest`, `StoreTicketTagRequest`, `StoreTicketSavedViewRequest`. Follow `app/Domains/Customers/Http/Requests/StoreCustomerRequest.php` (549 B) — `authorize()` delegating to the policy, `rules()` returning validation only. Route-key inputs are **uuids** (`customer_uuid`, `department_uuid`, `assignee_uuid`, `category_uuid`) resolved with `exists:…,uuid` rules; never accept numeric ids.

**Resources:** `TicketResource`, `TicketCategoryResource`, `TicketTagResource`, `TicketEventResource`, `TicketSavedViewResource` — modelled on `app/Domains/Customers/Http/Resources/CustomerResource.php` (907 B). Expose `uuid`, never `id` (`tests/Feature/Api/UuidExposureTest.php` enforces this). Bilingual category names render through `BilingualString` per `docs/contracts/localization.md`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Blocked customer.** Creating a ticket for a customer whose `status` is `blocked` (column defined at `create_customers_table.php` line 18) must fail with the existing blocked-customer error rather than a new one. Enforced in `CreateTicket` by delegating to `app/Domains/Customers/Services/CustomerIntakeGuard.php`.
- **Merged customer.** `Customer::resolveRouteBinding()` (`Customer.php` lines 76–97) transparently redirects to the surviving customer, and throws `ModelNotFoundException` after 10 hops (line 90). A ticket created against a merged uuid therefore lands on the **survivor** — assert this explicitly in tests so the behaviour is intentional, not accidental.
- **Concurrent creation.** Two simultaneous `POST /tickets` must not receive the same reference. Guaranteed by the transactional `lockForUpdate` in `TicketReferenceGenerator` plus the `tickets.reference` unique index. On a unique-violation retry **once**, then surface a 500 — do not loop indefinitely.
- **Never-reused references.** Deleting a ticket row must not decrement `ticket_references.last_sequence`. The generator reads only the counter table.
- **Category depth 4.** Attempting to create a child under a depth-3 category throws `TicketCategoryDepthExceededException` from `TicketCategoryTree::assertCanNest()` → 422.
- **Category cycle.** `parent_id` pointing at the category itself or a descendant must be rejected in `UpdateTicketCategory` before saving; the `ancestors()` walk is bounded to 3 hops so a corrupt row cannot hang a request.
- **Custom field for the wrong category.** Sending a key that belongs to a sibling category throws `InvalidTicketCustomFieldException` with the offending `field` in `errorMeta()`.
- **Reclassification orphans values.** Moving a ticket to a category that does not declare a previously-set key drops that value and records it in the `Reclassified` event payload — data loss must be visible in history.
- **Inactive category.** A category with `is_active = false` cannot be chosen for a **new** ticket, but existing tickets keep it and still render. Enforced in `StoreTicketRequest`/`CreateTicket`, not in the resource.
- **Arabic and unicode tags.** `ticket_tags.name_normalised` is unique after `ArabicTextNormaliser` processing, so alef variants and trailing whitespace collapse into a single tag while `name` preserves the first-seen display form. Empty or whitespace-only tag names are rejected.
- **Arabic search.** `q` must match a subject written with a bare alef when the stored subject uses a hamza-carrying alef, because both go through the same normaliser. `reference` matching is **not** normalised — it is ASCII and matched exactly (case-insensitive).
- **Very long body.** `body` is `text`; `body_normalised` is `text` and nullable. Cap normalisation input length in `TicketSearch` so a megabyte body cannot blow up the request; document the cap in a comment.
- **Empty list / empty counts.** When the filtered set is empty, `meta.counts.status` and `meta.counts.priority` are returned as **empty objects**, not `null` and not omitted — clients render zero-state from them.
- **Saved view referencing a deleted department or category.** The view still loads; the filter simply matches nothing. Do **not** 404 the list request because a stored filter value is stale.
- **Saved view of another user.** Loading a non-shared view owned by someone else returns 404 (not 403) so view ownership is not enumerable.
- **Unassigned tickets.** `assigned_user_id` is nullable and `filter[assignee]=none` must be supported to list them; deactivating a user (`app/Domains/Security/Actions/DeactivateUser.php`) must not orphan tickets — the FK is `nullOnDelete` and deactivation does not delete users.
- **History never derived.** A no-op `PATCH` (identical values) writes **no** `ticket_events` row. A second `PATCH` that genuinely changes one field writes exactly one row with exactly one entry in `payload.changes`.
- **Partial migration state.** `ticket_events`, `ticket_tag_ticket` and `ticket_tags` depend on `tickets`; running only part of the migration batch leaves FK creation failing loudly rather than silently. See Migration / Rollback below.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Order matters.** `ticket_categories` → `ticket_category_fields` → `ticket_references` → `tickets` → `ticket_tags`/`ticket_tag_ticket` → `ticket_events` → `ticket_saved_views`. The timestamp prefixes above encode this; do not renumber them.
- **Rollback** is `php artisan migrate:rollback --step=7`, which drops in reverse order. Each `down()` is a bare `Schema::dropIfExists(...)`, matching `create_customers_table.php` lines 27–30.
- **Half-applied state.** If `create_tickets_table` succeeds but `create_ticket_events_table` fails, tickets exist with no history table and `RecordTicketEvent` throws on every write — the API is hard-down rather than silently losing history, which is the intended failure mode. Re-run `php artisan migrate` after fixing; no data repair is needed because no tickets can be created in that state.
- **`ticket_references` is never truncated.** Document in the migration docblock that truncating it would allow reference reuse and violate the acceptance criteria. It must be excluded from any future test-data reset that is not a full `migrate:fresh`.
- **No data backfill** is required — all tables are new and start empty. `database/database.sqlite` is a dev artefact; run `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed` locally after pulling.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend migrates:** from the repo root, `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed` — completes with no FK errors and seeds the ticket catalogue tree.
2. **Static analysis:** `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse` (config at `phpstan.neon`) — no new errors in `app/Domains/Ticketing/`.
3. **Formatting:** `vendor/bin/pint --test` (or the equivalent target in `Makefile` — check `make` targets first).
4. **Unit tests:** `php artisan test --testsuite=Unit` from the repo root.
5. **Feature tests:** `php artisan test tests/Feature/Tickets`.
6. **Regression:** `php artisan test` — the full suite, with `tests/Feature/Api/UuidExposureTest.php`, `tests/Unit/Support/MassAssignmentAuditTest.php`, `tests/Unit/Support/ApiConventionsAuditTest.php` and `tests/Feature/Seeders/` green.
7. **Manual smoke:** `POST /api/v1/tickets` twice with the same idempotency key → one ticket, one reference; `GET /api/v1/tickets?q=<arabic-subject>` → the ticket is returned; `GET /api/v1/tickets/{uuid}/history` → the `Created` event with the acting user's uuid.

- [x] A ticket cannot be created without a **customer**, a **department** and a **priority**; `assigned_user_id` is nullable and an unassigned ticket is creatable and listable (`filter[assignee]=none`).
- [x] Every ticket receives a unique reference in the documented `TKT-YYYYMM-NNNNNN` format; references are **never reused**, proven by a test that deletes the latest ticket and allocates again.
- [x] `ticket_categories` supports a bilingual tree of **at most three levels**; a fourth level is rejected with a typed error and an entry in `lang/en/errors.php` and `lang/ar/errors.php`.
- [x] A category may declare custom fields; values are captured at creation, validated against the category chain, and stored in `tickets.custom_fields`.
- [x] Free-form tags can be attached and removed, are normalised for uniqueness, and `filter[tag]` narrows the ticket list.
- [x] `GET /api/v1/tickets` uses `CollectionQuerySpec`/`CollectionQuery` for sorting, filtering, includes and pagination, supports `?view={uuid}` saved views with request params taking precedence, and returns `meta.counts.status` and `meta.counts.priority`.
- [x] `q` matches subject, body and reference; Arabic variants match through the same `TextNormaliser`/`ArabicTextNormaliser` used by customer search, with **no** duplicated normalisation code.
- [x] Every meaningful mutation writes exactly one `ticket_events` row via `RecordTicketEvent` with actor, type, changed-field payload and `occurred_at`; a no-op update writes none; `GET /tickets/{ticket}/history` returns them newest-first.
- [x] New permission keys exist in `PermissionKey`, are seeded by `PermissionsAndRolesSeeder`, and are enforced by `TicketPolicy`/`TicketCategoryPolicy` registered in `AppServiceProvider`.
- [x] No API response exposes a numeric primary key; all ticket routes bind on `uuid`.
- [x] All new and existing tests pass; `phpstan` and `pint --test` are clean.
